raidSayLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Luis Lopez. Emergency dispatcher. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Father's Whetstone, Field suture kit, Daughter's Drawing, Dead Phone, Dispatcher's headset. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire
A person, maybe 30s, with a wiry build: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
